reproducibility.label: measured 2026-07-30 on a dedicated GCP T4 (n1-standard-8, us-central1-a, sole tenant, persistence mode on, SM clock locked to 1590 MHz), TensorRT 10.3.0

second_run.outcome: SUPERSEDED by the 2026-07-30 dedicated-T4 run in this file. This shared vast.ai instance measured every model 17-85% slower and concluded the 4.0-7.1 ms source band was 'NOT portable across T4 instances'. That conclusion was WRONG: it was neighbour contention, not hardware variation. Re-measuring the md5-identical ONNX on a sole-tenant T4 with locked clocks and the SAME TensorRT 10.3.0 moved DEIM-M 43.00 -> 6.61 ms (the source T4 recorded 6.56), YOLOX-M 14.76 -> 5.70, YOLO26m 12.99 -> 5.85, RTMDet-M 17.01 -> 8.19, DAMO-YOLO-M 11.75 -> 6.70. The two in-graph-decode DETRs moved least (RF-DETR 9.33 -> 7.71, RT-DETRv2 9.55 -> 7.93, both -17%), consistent with contention penalising the multi-kernel dense-head/NMS paths hardest. Retained as evidence of the contention effect, not as a competing measurement.
